checks: 2 failure rows with independently re-derived classification, decision and executed action
observation layer carries typed fields only; Retry-After normalized, no raw header, URL or free text
one RecoveryChain ledger per failed owner; refresh and provider wait spend no REMOTE_ATTEMPT
2 REMOTE_ATTEMPT charges == 2 physical attempts; 3 origin requests accounted
binding-1 replaced by binding-2 for the same immutable FetchKey and extent identity
one refresh operation, one refresh charge; no revision reused or derived from material
provider-directed Retry-After used as-is: 2000 ms wait, no extra backoff
deterministic provider simulator fault attribution: one stale-binding signal, one refresh success

limitations: M2-D proves provider-neutral delivery-binding replacement, Retry-After handling and deterministic provider recovery.

It does not by itself prove that a live YouTube HTTP 403 means an expired binding, does not select a production YouTube client/profile, does not implement SABR/PO-token/challenge handling, and does not select the production transport.
